Job Overview

As an Accounts Payable Accountant at Gotion, Inc., you will be responsible for managing the company's incoming financial obligations. You will ensure timely and accurate processing of vendor invoices, maintaining effective relationships with suppliers, and supporting the overall financial operations of the company.

Responsibilities

  • Manage the payment schedule and ensure timely payments to vendors.

  • Reconcile vendor statements and resolve discrepancies.

  • Assist with month-end and year-end closing procedures.

  • Maintain and update the accounts payable system for accurate financial reporting.

  • Respond to inquiries from vendors and internal departments regarding invoices and payments.

  • Support audits by providing necessary documentation and reports.

  • Assist in streamlining AP processes and improving efficiency.

  • Handle tax-related matters and support compliance with local, state, and federal regulations.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.

  • Minimum of 2 years of experience in accounts payable or a similar financial role.

  • Strong knowledge of accounting principles and AP processes.

  • Proficiency in accounting software (e.g., QuickBooks, SAP) and Microsoft Excel.

  • High attention to detail and accuracy.

  • Strong communication and problem-solving skills.

Administration Director

Location: U.S. Manufacturing Facility
Level: Director
Reports to: Head of Management Center
Site Size: Approximately 500 employees

Position Summary

The Plant Administration Director is responsible for leading the overall administrative operations and site services for a manufacturing facility of approximately 500 employees.

This role ensures the safe, efficient, professional, and cost-effective operation of the site by overseeing general administration, employee services, security, transportation, catering, facility support, vendor management, workplace services, executive/VIP visits, and major site events.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on site leader with strong experience supporting large-scale manufacturing operations and building effective administrative systems in a fast-paced environment.

Key Responsibilities

1. Plant Administration & Site Operations

  • Lead the overall day-to-day administrative operations and site services for a manufacturing facility of approximately 500 employees.
  • Develop, implement, and continuously improve administrative policies, procedures, service standards, and operating processes.
  • Ensure administrative services effectively support production schedules, shift operations, and overall plant requirements.
  • Identify operational issues and drive timely resolution in coordination with relevant departments.
  • Develop annual administration plans, budgets, and cost-control initiatives.

2. Employee & Workplace Services

  • Oversee employee services including catering, transportation/shuttle services, accommodation support, uniforms, office supplies, meeting rooms, mail/courier services, and other workplace services.
  • Ensure administrative resources are appropriately adjusted based on workforce growth, production schedules, and shift requirements.
  • Establish service standards and employee feedback mechanisms to continuously improve the employee experience.

3. Site & Facility Support

  • Oversee administrative management of office areas, common areas, and plant support facilities.
  • Manage janitorial services, landscaping, snow removal, waste services, pest control, and other general site services.
  • Partner closely with Facilities, Engineering, EHS, Production, and Maintenance teams to ensure site issues are resolved efficiently.
  • Maintain a professional, organized, and operationally ready workplace environment.

4. Security & Site Access

  • Oversee plant security operations, including security vendors, access control, visitor management, vehicle access, site patrols, and restricted-area management.
  • Establish and maintain effective visitor and contractor management procedures.
  • Coordinate with EHS and plant leadership on emergency response and business continuity activities related to site administration.

5. Vendor & Contract Management

  • Manage administrative vendors and service providers, including catering, transportation, security, janitorial, accommodation, and workplace service providers.
  • Establish and monitor vendor KPIs and SLAs related to quality, cost, compliance, responsiveness, and service performance.
  • Conduct regular vendor performance reviews and drive corrective actions when required.
  • Identify opportunities for cost reduction, contract optimization, and service improvement.

6. Executive Visits & Major Events

  • Lead administrative coordination for executive visits, customer visits, government delegations, business partners, and other VIP guests.
  • Plan and support major plant meetings, employee events, celebrations, community events, and corporate activities.
  • Establish professional and standardized protocols for VIP reception and plant tours.

7. Cross-Functional Coordination

  • Partner closely with HR, EHS, Production, Engineering, Finance, Procurement, IT, and other functions to support plant operations.
  • Lead cross-functional resolution of administrative and site service issues.
  • Support relationships with local service providers, community organizations, government agencies, and other external stakeholders as needed.

8. Team Leadership

  • Lead and develop the plant administration team, including organization design, staffing, performance management, and capability development.
  • Establish clear team responsibilities, KPIs, service standards, and accountability mechanisms.
  • Build a professional, responsive, service-oriented administration organization capable of supporting continued plant growth.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Management, Operations, Hospitality Management, or a related field preferred.
  • 10+ years of progressive administration, hotel management, site operations, or general affairs experience, preferably within a manufacturing environment.
  • 5+ years of people management experience, with demonstrated ability to lead multidisciplinary administrative teams.
  • Develop and maintain effective relationships with local, and state government agencies and officials, serving as a key company representative on government and regulatory matters impacting site operations.
  • Experience supporting a 300–1,000+ employee manufacturing facility strongly preferred.
  • Strong knowledge of plant administration, employee services, security, transportation, catering, workplace services, and vendor management.
  • Demonstrated experience in budget management, cost control, contract negotiation, and vendor performance management.
  • Strong organizational, problem-solving, and cross-functional leadership skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and respond effectively to urgent site operational issues.
  • Strong executive presence and communication skills, with the ability to interact effectively with senior leadership, employees, vendors, customers, and external stakeholders.
  • Experience in battery, EV, automotive, semiconductor, energy, or other advanced manufacturing industries preferred.
  • Experience working in a multicultural and international organization is highly desirable.
  • Bilingual English/Mandarin communication skills are a plus.

title: Associate Director, Module & Pack Rework
description:
Gotion Inc. is based in Silicon Valley, CA, currently building a Manufacturing facility in Manteno, IL and has R&D centers in Ohio, China, Japan and Europe. We innovate in the next generation electric vehicle and energy storage technologies (lithium batteries and related systems) with the aim to accelerate electrified transportation and achieve sustainable development. Gotion is powered by a leading power battery technology company that provides solutions for vehicles including the world's first mass commercial e-bus route.

Gotion is a career destination - we are not simply attempting to just fill another job, but to pursue a dream of global green energy together! We offer outstanding opportunities to individuals seeking an exciting and challenging working environment. Everyone is highly valued and plays a vital role in the growth of our organization.

Position Summary

We are seeking an experienced Associate Director, Module & Pack Rework, to lead the end-to-end rework, repair, recovery, testing, and disposition of lithium-ion battery modules and packs. This role will build and manage a safe, standardized, scalable, and data-driven rework operation supporting high-volume battery manufacturing.

The ideal candidate brings strong manufacturing leadership, battery module/pack knowledge, quality systems expertise, technical troubleshooting, and continuous improvement experience. This position partners across Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, Maintenance, Planning, Logistics, EHS, and suppliers to maximize recovery, reduce scrap, improve throughput, and prevent recurring defects.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead all Module and Pack rework operations, including defect evaluation, repair, validation testing, quality release, and final disposition.
  • Build and scale the rework organization, including staffing, equipment, capacity planning, workflows, and operating strategy.
  • Establish standardized procedures, repair limits, quality standards, traceability, escalation paths, and controls for nonconforming product.
  • Own daily performance across safety, quality, delivery, cost, inventory, recovery rate, cycle time, and throughput.
  • Analyze defect and performance data, drive corrective actions, and provide regular updates to leadership.

Rework Process & Quality Management

  • Develop and continuously improve standardized rework processes for diagnosis, component replacement, electrical/mechanical repair, software verification, validation testing, and final release.
  • Ensure reworked products meet the same safety, quality, reliability, and functional requirements as standard production units.
  • Partner with Quality to define acceptance criteria, repair limits, scrap thresholds, MRB disposition, deviations, and concessions.
  • Establish defect tracking and reporting systems to measure repair effectiveness, reliability, recurrence, and recovery performance.
  • Lead root cause investigations, 8D/CAPA activities, and closure of recurring manufacturing and quality issues.

Manufacturing & Engineering Coordination

  • Lead cross-functional troubleshooting of Module and Pack manufacturing defects and drive corrective actions across processes, equipment, tooling, and production controls.
  • Support diagnostic, automation, testing, MES, and traceability solutions that improve rework efficiency and decision-making.
  • Partner with internal teams and equipment suppliers to resolve technical issues and support production launches and ramp-ups.

Continuous Improvement & Cost Reduction

  • Reduce scrap, rework cost, and Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ) by prioritizing high-impact defect and manufacturing loss reduction.
  • Improve yield, recovery rate, cycle time, labor efficiency, equipment uptime, and defect recurrence through Lean and data-driven improvement.
  • Optimize workflow, material flow, tooling, and repair methods; quantify savings and drive long-term defect elimination at the source.

Production, Workforce & Material Control

  • Build, lead, and develop a high-performing rework team with clear staffing plans, production targets, roles, responsibilities, and escalation processes.
  • Develop training and qualification programs for battery rework, troubleshooting, quality standards, and safe work practices.
  • Coordinate identification, segregation, traceability, storage, inventory, and movement of nonconforming products, replacement parts, and repair materials.
  • Foster a culture of safety, accountability, teamwork, ownership, and continuous improvement.

Safety & Compliance

  • Ensure all rework activities comply with EHS, regulatory, and company requirements.
  • Establish and enforce safe practices for lithium-ion battery handling, electrical safety, LOTO, PPE, and hazardous material controls.
  • Partner with EHS on risk assessments, controls, and personnel qualification for battery rework operations.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, or a related field.
  • 5+ years of manufacturing, engineering, quality, or operations experience, including leadership responsibility.
  • Strong experience in manufacturing operations, technical troubleshooting, process improvement, and quality systems.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead teams and deliver results in a fast-paced production environment.

Technical Skills

  • Knowledge of lithium-ion battery systems, manufacturing processes, testing, and safety.
  • Experience with automated equipment, PLC/HMI systems, robotics, MES, and traceability systems.
  • Proficiency in Root Cause Analysis, 8D, PFMEA, CAPA, Lean Manufacturing, and continuous improvement tools.

Core Competencies

  • Leadership and team development
  • Problem-solving and decision-making
  • Cross-functional collaboration
  • Continuous improvement
  • Safety / Quality / Delivery / Cost ownership
  • Data-driven execution

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in battery, EV, automotive, energy storage, or other high-volume manufacturing environments.
  • Experience with battery Module/Pack production, rework operations, production line launches, or manufacturing scale-up.
  • Lean Six Sigma, PMP, or similar certification preferred.

Job Title: HR Business Partner / Employee Relations Specialist

Location: Manteno, IL

Work Schedule: Fully On-site, Monday–Friday

Employment Type: Full-time

Experience Level: 5–10 years

Language Requirement: English and Spanish bilingual required

About the Role

Gotion is seeking a hands-on HR Business Partner / Employee Relations Specialist to support our business and R&D teams in Manteno, Illinois. This role is designed for an execution-oriented HR professional who can work closely with managers and employees on employee relations, 90-day reviews, performance management, documentation, corrective actions, investigations, and day-to-day HR support.

This is a fully on-site role, Monday through Friday. The ideal candidate should be comfortable working directly with business leaders, technical managers, R&D teams, and employees in a fast-paced, cross-functional environment.

Key Responsibilities

Lead and support employee relations matters, including employee complaints, workplace concerns, misconduct issues, communication conflicts, attendance concerns, policy violations, and manager-employee disputes.

Conduct workplace investigations, document findings, summarize facts, and recommend appropriate next steps in partnership with HR leadership and management.

Support the 90-day review process for new hires, including review tracking, manager follow-up, documentation, performance feedback, and employment decision support.

Partner with business and R&D managers on performance management, including coaching conversations, performance documentation, corrective action, PIP support, and follow-up actions.

Maintain strong on-site visibility and build effective working relationships with employees, managers, and cross-functional stakeholders.

Provide Spanish-language HR support when needed, including policy explanation, employee communication, investigation interviews, coaching, and issue resolution.

Ensure consistent application of company policies, performance standards, attendance expectations, disciplinary processes, and workplace conduct requirements.

Prepare and maintain accurate HR documentation, including investigation notes, corrective action forms, 90-day review records, performance documentation, and employee relations case files.

Coach managers on handling difficult employee conversations in a compliant, practical, and well-documented manner.

Partner with HR leadership, legal, payroll, operations, and functional leaders on employee relations, performance, compliance, leave, attendance, and workforce management issues.

Identify recurring ER or performance issues and recommend practical improvements to reduce risk, improve accountability, and strengthen team effectiveness.

Support additional HR activities as needed, including onboarding, employee communication, HR reporting, policy rollout, employee engagement, and manager enablement.

Required Qualifications

5–10 years of HR experience, with strong hands-on experience in employee relations, performance management, corrective actions, workplace investigations, and manager coaching.

Prior experience supporting business, technical, R&D, engineering, commercial, project, or cross-functional teams.

Fluent or professional working proficiency in both English and Spanish.

Strong understanding of employee relations documentation, investigation processes, corrective action, attendance management, and performance review processes.

Ability to work fully on-site in Manteno, IL, Monday through Friday.

Comfortable working directly with managers, employees, technical teams, and business leaders.

Strong judgment, confidentiality, documentation discipline, and ability to handle sensitive employee matters.

Ability to operate in a fast-paced environment where HR must be visible, responsive, practical, and execution-focused.

Strong communication skills, including the ability to explain policies, expectations, and performance feedback clearly in both English and Spanish.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting 90-day reviews, probationary period evaluations, structured new-hire performance reviews, or manager-led performance calibration.

Experience supporting R&D, engineering, product, commercial, sales, project management, or technical business teams.

Experience in battery, EV, clean energy, automotive, technology, advanced manufacturing, or high-growth industrial environments.

Knowledge of Illinois employment practices and general U.S. employment law principles.

Experience with HRIS, case tracking, attendance systems, performance documentation systems, or employee relations case management tools.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate is a practical, on-site HR operator who can support business and R&D teams with discipline, speed, and sound judgment. This person should be able to handle employee relations cases independently, follow through on 90-day reviews and performance actions, coach managers through difficult conversations, and keep documentation clean and defensible.

This role is best suited for someone who is not looking for a purely strategic HR role. We need someone who can execute, follow up, document, communicate clearly, and help managers build accountability across the organization.

Compensation

Compensation will be based on experience, qualifications, and internal equity.

Work Location

Manteno, IL

Fully on-site, Monday–Friday

Language Requirement

English and Spanish bilingual required.

Job Description

Inventory Control Specialist

Position Summary

The Inventory Control Specialist is responsible for maintaining accurate inventory records, ensuring inventory integrity, and supporting warehouse and production operations through effective inventory management practices. This position works closely with Warehouse, Production, Logistics, Purchasing, Quality, and Finance teams to ensure timely and accurate inventory transactions, reconciliation, reporting, and compliance with company procedures.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Inventory Management

  • Monitor and maintain inventory accuracy within ERP/WMS systems.
  • Process inventory transactions including receipts, transfers, adjustments, returns, and shipments.
  • Perform daily inventory reconciliation and investigate inventory discrepancies.
  • Conduct cycle counts and support physical inventory activities.
  • Analyze inventory variances and identify root causes.
  • Recommend corrective actions to prevent recurring inventory issues.

ERP/WMS Operations

  • Ensure all inventory transactions are accurately recorded in ERP and Warehouse Management Systems.
  • Review and validate inventory data integrity.
  • Support system troubleshooting and resolve inventory-related transaction errors.
  • Assist with ERP/WMS process improvements and optimization initiatives.

Cross-Functional Coordination

  • Coordinate with Production teams to ensure material availability and inventory accuracy.
  • Collaborate with Logistics and Warehouse teams regarding material movement and inventory transactions.
  • Partner with Purchasing and Supply Chain teams to resolve receiving and inventory discrepancies.
  • Support Finance during inventory reconciliation and month-end closing activities.

Reporting and Analysis

  • Prepare daily, weekly, and monthly inventory reports.
  • Track inventory KPIs including inventory accuracy, inventory aging, cycle count performance, and material shortages.
  • Analyze inventory trends and provide recommendations for improvement.
  • Support management with inventory performance metrics and operational reporting.

Compliance and Audit Support

  • Ensure compliance with company inventory control policies and procedures.
  • Maintain documentation supporting inventory transactions and adjustments.
  • Assist with internal and external audits.
  • Support implementation of inventory control best practices and continuous improvement initiatives.

Continuous Improvement

  • Identify opportunities to improve inventory accuracy and operational efficiency.
  • Participate in warehouse and supply chain improvement projects.
  • Support Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement activities.

Qualifications

Education

  • Associate’s Degree or Bachelor’s Degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Business Administration, Operations Management, or a related field preferred.

Experience

  • Minimum 3 years of inventory control, warehouse operations, logistics, or supply chain experience in a manufacturing environment.
  • Experience with ERP systems (SAP preferred).
  • Experience using Warehouse Management Systems (WMS).
  • Battery manufacturing, automotive, or high-volume manufacturing experience preferred.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Strong understanding of inventory control principles and warehouse operations.
  • Proficiency with ERP and WMS systems.
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  • Ability to investigate and resolve inventory discrepancies.
  • Excellent communication and cross-functional coordination skills.
  • Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities.
  • Detail-oriented with a high degree of accuracy.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to work in a warehouse and manufacturing environment.
  • Ability to stand, walk, and move throughout the facility for extended periods.
  • Ability to occasionally lift up to 25 pounds.
  • Ability to perform cycle counts and physical inventory verification activities.

Working Conditions

  • Manufacturing and warehouse environment.
  • May require occasional overtime, weekend work, or support during physical inventory activities.

description:

Role Summary:

The Maintenance Technician is responsible for installing, troubleshooting, repairing, and maintaining production equipment, automated systems, robotic cells, forklifts, facility systems, and associated electrical, mechanical, pneumatic, and hydraulic components. This position supports safe, efficient, and reliable plant operations through preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance activities.

The ideal candidate possesses strong mechanical aptitude, industrial electrical troubleshooting skills, and experience working with automated manufacturing equipment in a fast-paced production environment.

 

Responsibilities (includes but not limited to):

  • Troubleshoot, repair, and maintain mechanical, electrical, pneumatic, and hydraulic systems on production equipment and facility assets.
  • Diagnose and repair industrial electrical systems, including motors, controls, sensors, VFDs, and 480V three-phase equipment.
  • Perform preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance to maximize equipment reliability and minimize downtime.
  • Maintain and support robotic cells, automated machinery, conveyors, forklifts, and material handling equipment.
  • Read and interpret electrical schematics, mechanical drawings, and pneumatic/hydraulic diagrams to identify and resolve equipment issues.
  • Handling and dismantling battery packs and modules
  • Install, modify, and upgrade machinery, equipment, and plant systems as required to support operational goals.
  • Follow all safety procedures, including Lockout/Tagout (LOTO), machine guarding, and electrical safety standards while maintaining accurate maintenance records.

 

Requirements

  • High School Diploma or GED required.
  • Extensive experience in industrial maintenance experience in a manufacturing environment.
  • Strong troubleshooting skills in mechanical, electrical, pneumatic, and hydraulic systems.
  • Experience working with 120V, 240V, and 480V industrial electrical systems.
  • Ability to read and interpret electrical, mechanical, pneumatic, and hydraulic schematics.
  • Experience using diagnostic equipment including multimeters, clamp meters, and test instruments.
  • Proficient with hand tools, power tools, and precision measuring devices.
  • Ability to work independently and prioritize multiple tasks.

 

Desired Qualifications:

  • Technical degree or certification in Industrial Maintenance, Mechatronics, Electrical Technology, or related field.
  • PLC troubleshooting experience (Allen-Bradley, Siemens, or similar).
  • Experience with industrial robots (FANUC, ABB, Yaskawa, KUKA, etc.).
  • Forklift maintenance experience.
  • Welding and fabrication experience.
  • Knowledge of CMMS systems.
  • OSHA 10 or OSHA 30 certification.
  • Certified Maintenance & Reliability Technician (CMRT) or similar credential.

 

Physical Requirements

  • Frequently stand, walk, bend, kneel, climb, and work in industrial environments.
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds regularly and up to 75 pounds occasionally with assistance.
  • Ability to work from ladders, lifts, platforms, and elevated heights.
  • Ability to work in varying temperatures, noise levels, and production conditions.
  • Ability to distinguish wire colors and perform detailed troubleshooting activities.

description:
Gotion Inc. is based in Silicon Valley, CA, currently building a Manufacturing facility in Manteno, IL and has R&D centers in Ohio, China, Japan and Europe. We innovate in the next generation electric vehicle and energy storage technologies (lithium batteries and related systems) with the aim to accelerate electrified transportation and achieve sustainable development. Pack Performance Engineer 

Battery Systems / Pack Engineering 

Department:  Battery Systems / Pack Engineering 

Reports to:  Head of Battery Systems Engineering (or Pack Engineering Lead) 

Level:  Senior / Staff Engineer 

Location:  United States (site aligned to Gotion's North America engineering footprint) 

 

Role Summary 

The Pack Performance Engineer owns the technical bridge between cell, BMS, and vehicle: defining and validating how a battery pack performs across its power boundaries, thermal envelope, and system requirements. This is a hybrid role that sits deliberately at the intersection of three disciplines — BMS/controls, systems engineering, and pack hardware/thermal — rather than living entirely inside one. You will define power and SOC/SOP limits and see them through to vehicle integration, translate performance requirements into validated system attributes, and own pack-level thermal and hardware performance from design through DVP. 

Core Focus Areas 

1. BMS Interface, Power Limits & Vehicle Integration 

  • Define battery charge/discharge current limits, combining SOC, temperature, and cell capability to establish accurate power boundaries 
  • Own SOC estimation and SOP (state of power) algorithm inputs and validation 
  • Lead cell balancing strategy and isolation measurement verification 
  • Drive BMS and Vehicle Control Unit (VCU) integration, ensuring pack performance data and limits are correctly interpreted at the vehicle level 
  • Support functional safety testing and requirements across chemistries (e.g. NCM, LFP) 
  • Assess the impact of production ramp, design changes, and process changes on battery system performance 

 

2. Battery System Requirements & Performance Validation 

  • Translate electrified-powertrain architecture and performance targets into clear, traceable battery system requirements 
  • Own performance-attribute definition and specification across the battery system 
  • Build and maintain functional safety traceability from requirement to validation 
  • Lead systems-level validation planning and execution across battery systems, requirements, and vehicle integration 
  • Partner with powertrain, controls, and vehicle integration teams to keep requirements and validation evidence aligned 

 

3. Pack Hardware Performance & Thermal Management 

  • Own pack-level performance evaluation: available power, internal resistance, and thermal performance 
  • Provide pack performance input into BMS configuration 
  • Lead battery performance testing including thermal cycling, thermal runaway characterization, and DVP (Design Verification Plan) execution 
  • Support custom high-voltage battery pack design, prototype build, and validation 
  • Own pack thermal / cooling system development, from concept through validated performance 
  • Analyze capacity, DCIR, cell-disconnect behavior and other pack-level performance data to inform design decisions 

Required Experience & Qualifications 

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field 
  • 7+ years of experience in battery systems, BMS, or pack engineering at an EV OEM or battery systems supplier 
  • Hands-on experience with SOC/SOP estimation, cell balancing, and isolation measurement 
  • Demonstrated experience defining charge/discharge current limits and power boundaries across SOC, temperature, and cell capability 
  • BMS and Vehicle Control Unit (VCU) integration experience 
  • Experience defining battery system requirements and performance attributes, with functional safety traceability 
  • Experience with pack thermal design and validation — thermal cycling, thermal runaway, and DVP 
  • Experience with high-voltage battery pack design, prototyping, and validation 
  • Working familiarity with multiple cell chemistries (e.g. NCM, LFP) 
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration skills across systems, controls, hardware, and vehicle integration teams 

Preferred 

  • A demonstrated “T-shaped” background spanning both BMS/controls and pack hardware/thermal domains, rather than depth in only one 
  • Experience in a high-volume EV production environment, including support through production ramp 
  • Direct ownership of functional safety (ISO 26262) traceability from requirement to validation 
  • Prior experience at an EV OEM or battery systems integrator (e.g. supporting passenger, commercial, or energy storage platforms) 

 

This role profile reflects a converged target persona validated against real market benchmarks across BMS/vehicle-integration, systems/requirements, and pack-hardware/thermal backgrounds. It is intended as a working draft for hiring-manager review before search begins.

description:

About Gotion 

Gotion Inc. is a global leader in next-generation energy storage and electric vehicle technologies, specializing in lithium batteries and related systems. Headquartered in Silicon Valley, California, Gotion is expanding its manufacturing footprint with a state-of-the-art facility in Manteno, Illinois, and operates research and development centers across Ohio, China, Japan, and Europe. 
 
Driven by innovation and a commitment to sustainability, Gotion develops advanced battery solutions that power electric vehicles and energy storage systems around the world. Backed by industry-leading battery technology, Gotion continues to advance the future of electrified transportation and support the global transition to clean energy. 
 
At Gotion, we believe our people are the driving force behind our success. We are more than a workplace—we are a team united by a shared mission to build a more sustainable future. Every employee is empowered to contribute, innovate, and grow while making a meaningful impact. 
 
If you are looking for more than just a job—if you are seeking an opportunity to help shape the future of global green energy—we invite you to build that future with us. 

Our Culture 

At Gotion, we value collaboration, respect, continuous learning, and innovation. We work in a dynamic, multicultural environment where diverse perspectives strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and deliver sustainable energy solutions. Our core values—Care, Pragmatism, Integrity, and Innovation—guide how we work together, serve our customers, and build the future. 

Position Summary 

Gotion is seeking a Principal Structural & CAE Durability Engineer to lead structural integrity, fatigue, and durability analysis for battery module and pack systems supporting next-generation EV and energy storage programs. This senior technical leadership role owns the CAE strategy, analysis methods, and automation roadmap for structural and durability engineering, mentors engineers across the team, and partners closely with Design Release Engineers (DREs) and cross-functional engineering groups to ensure battery structural designs meet performance, reliability, and manufacturability requirements. The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in FEA-based structural and durability analysis, a proven track record developing analysis automation tools, and experience applying AI/ML techniques to advance CAE capability. 

Gotion Core Values 

  • Care: Demonstrates respect, empathy, professionalism, safety, quality, teamwork, and customer focus. 
  • Pragmatism: Makes practical, data-driven decisions that balance quality, efficiency, cost, and business needs. 
  • Integrity: Acts honestly and ethically while maintaining confidentiality and compliance with company policies and laws. 
  • Innovation: Continuously seeks better ideas, technologies, and processes to improve business performance. 

Essential Duties & Responsibilities 

  • Lead structural, fatigue, durability, and NVH CAE analysis for battery module and pack designs, including vibration fatigue (random PSD, sine dwell/sweep), weld fatigue (spot, laser, staple, MIG), and thermal cycling creep/fatigue of polymeric components.
    • Define and drive the structural/CAE analysis strategy, methods, and technology roadmap across battery engineering programs.
    • Develop and implement automation tools and standard engineering work processes to improve CAE modeling quality, efficiency, and repeatability. 
    • Apply optimization, DOE, and AI/ML techniques to guide battery module and pack design decisions. 
    • Partner closely with Design Release Engineers (DREs) and cross-functional teams (mechanical, electrical, systems, manufacturing) to ensure structural designs meet performance, safety, and reliability targets. 
    • Review and validate FEA models, structural calculations, and analysis reports for battery components including trays, cell tabs, BDU, ICB, side plates, and brackets. 
    • Lead root cause investigations of structural failures, test findings, and field issues, and support corrective action development. 
    • Evaluate and implement CAE software/platforms and tools (e.g., ABAQUS, HyperWorks/OptiStruct, NASTRAN, LS-DYNA, ANSA, nCode) to support analysis needs. 
    • Mentor and provide technical leadership to structural and CAE engineers across the team. 
    • Present analysis results, design recommendations, and program-level structural risk assessments to engineering and program leadership. 
    • Support continuous improvement of engineering standards, design practices, and simulation methodology. 
    • Other duties as assigned. 

Supervisory Responsibilities 

This position does not have direct reports but is expected to provide technical leadership, mentorship, and analysis review guidance to structural and CAE engineers across programs. 

Required Qualifications 

  • PhD or MS in Mechanical Engineering, Structural Engineering, Solid Mechanics, or a related technical discipline.
    • 15+ years of experience in structural, fatigue, and durability CAE analysis, ideally within automotive, battery, or related industrial systems.
    • Expert-level proficiency in FEA and CAE tools such as ABAQUS, HyperWorks/OptiStruct, NASTRAN, LS-DYNA, ANSA, and nCode. 
    • Strong background in fatigue, NVH, optimization/DOE, and multi-physics structural analysis. 
    • Proven track record developing CAE automation tools and standard engineering work processes. 
    • Experience with scripting/programming for CAE automation (Python, C/C++, Tcl/Tk, VBA, or similar). 
    • Demonstrated ability to define technical strategy, mentor engineers, and drive cross-functional collaboration. 
    • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience presenting to engineering and program leadership. 

Preferred Qualifications 

  • PhD in Mechanical Engineering or Solid Mechanics.
    • Direct experience with battery module/pack structural design and durability analysis.
    • Experience applying AI/ML techniques to CAE modeling and design optimization. 
    • Experience with Teamcenter/NX or similar PLM/CAD-integration environments. 
    • Track record of patents, publications, or industry recognition in structural/CAE engineering. 
    • Design for Six Sigma or related quality/process certification. 

Disclaimer

title: Sales Electrical Engineer
description:
Gotion Inc. is based in Silicon Valley, CA, currently building a Manufacturing facility in Manteno, IL and has R&D centers in Ohio, China, Japan and Europe. We innovate in the next generation electric vehicle and energy storage technologies (lithium batteries and related systems) with the aim to accelerate electrified transportation and achieve sustainable development. Role Summary:

The Sales Electrical Engineer is a hybrid commercial and technical role within the Market Management Center at Gotion Illinois New Energy. This position bridges the gap between engineering and business development — supporting customer acquisition and account management on the commercial side while providing the technical depth needed to configure, specify, and validate energy storage and power systems solutions. The ideal candidate is equally comfortable presenting a value proposition to a prospective customer as they are reviewing single-line diagrams, interpreting interconnection requirements, or working through system performance data with an engineering team. 

Key Responsibilities:

Sales & Customer Development 

  • Identify, qualify, and pursue new customer opportunities across target segments including C&I, data centers, municipalities, and utilities. 
  • Lead customer-facing engagements from initial outreach through proposal, negotiation, and contract execution. 
  • Develop and present tailored proposals that clearly communicate technical capabilities, financial value, and project structure. 
  • Build and maintain a pipeline of active prospects; track activity and report progress against sales targets to the Director. 
  • Support the development of marketing materials, capability decks, and case studies that position Gotion's BESS and energy solutions competitively. 
  • Represent Gotion at industry events, trade shows, and customer meetings as a credible technical and commercial voice. 

Technical Engineering Support 

  • Provide technical guidance on BESS system design, including sizing, configuration, power conversion, and grid interconnection requirements. 
  • Review and interpret single-line diagrams, protection relay schemes, and interconnection studies to support customer projects and internal deployments. 
  • Work with ComEd, PJM, and other utilities on interconnection applications, protection coordination studies, and technical compliance requirements — including THD/PQ testing and IEEE 519 compliance documentation. 
  • Collaborate with the Program Manager and Power Station Manager on technical specifications, equipment selection, and system commissioning. 
  • Evaluate and respond to customer technical due diligence requests, RFPs, and RFIs with accurate, well-documented answers. 
  • Support FEOC compliance documentation and domestic content analysis as needed for ITC qualification and customer-facing reporting. 

Cross-Functional Collaboration 

  • Act as the primary technical liaison between the Market Management Center and Gotion's engineering teams in the US and China. 
  • Translate customer and market requirements into clear technical briefs for internal engineering and product teams. 
  • Support hub expansion planning by providing technical input on site-specific design requirements for domestic and international deployments. 
  • Coordinate with outside legal counsel and government relations on technical aspects of permitting, MOU negotiations, and regulatory filings. 
  • Assist with aftersales support and warranty coordination, serving as a technical point of contact for existing customers post-COD. 

Minimum Qualifications (Required):

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Systems, or a closely related field. 
  • 4+ years of experience in electrical engineering, with at least 1–2 years in a customer-facing, sales engineering, or business development capacity. 
  • Working knowledge of power systems fundamentals: protection schemes, single-line diagrams, load flow, and interconnection standards. 
  • Familiarity with battery energy storage systems (BESS), inverters/PCS, and grid-tied or behind-the-meter energy applications. 
  • Demonstrated ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear, compelling language for non-technical audiences. 
  • Strong proposal writing, presentation, and customer communication skills. 
  • Proficiency in MS Office; experience with CRM tools and engineering software (AutoCAD, ETAP, or equivalent) is a plus. 

Preferred Qualifications (Nice to Have):

  • Experience with utility-scale BESS, solar-plus-storage, or grid services projects in PJM or MISO markets. 
  • Familiarity with ComEd interconnection processes, IEEE 519 harmonic distortion standards, and protection coordination studies. 
  • Understanding of PPA structures, capacity markets, ancillary services, and energy arbitrage fundamentals. 
  • Experience working with C&I customers, data centers, municipalities, or industrial energy buyers. 
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license or active pursuit of licensure. 
  • Bilingual (English/Mandarin) is a plus but not required

Additional Information:

  • This position is primarily based at the Manteno, Illinois facility with regular on-site presence expected. 
  • Travel to customer sites, utility offices, industry events, and partner facilities will be required — estimated 20–30% of the time. 
  • Occasional international travel to Gotion facilities in China or other global locations may arise as the business expands

description:

Key Responsibilities: 

  • Serve as the lead technical interface for U.S. OEM customers on battery cell design, development, validation, and industrialization. 
  • Provide technical leadership in customer discussions covering cell architecture, materials, electrochemical performance, safety, lifetime, fast charging, and manufacturability. 
  • Represent Gotion’s cell design and manufacturing capabilities, technology roadmap, product portfolio, and development maturity to OEM customers. 
  • Translate customer vehicle-, pack-, and system-level requirements into cell-level design requirements, targets, and engineering trade-offs. 
  • Build a deep understanding of customer applications, duty cycles, operating environments, and pack constraints to guide optimal cell and pack integration. 
  • Develop cell design solutions that balance energy density, power capability, safety, durability, cost, and manufacturing feasibility. 
  • Lead technical alignment with customers on cell requirements, design specifications, interface definitions, validation plans, and acceptance criteria. 
  • Lead cell design reviews, technical workshops, and engineering discussions with customers and internal teams from RFI/RFQ through development, launch, and mass production. 
  • Develop test methods and validation strategies to evaluate cell-level and cell-in-pack performance, safety, reliability, and durability. 
  • Analyze and interpret cell test data to assess design performance, identify technical risks, and recommend design improvements. 
  • Lead root-cause investigations and corrective actions for cell design, performance, safety, and manufacturing issues; clearly communicate findings and recommendations to customers. 
  • Provide technical leadership throughout the complete cell development lifecycle, including concept development, design optimization, design verification, manufacturing scale-up, launch, and post-launch improvement. 
  • Collaborate with cross functional teams to develop DFMEAs and PFMEAs, identify critical design and process characteristics, and coordinate FMEA reviews with customers. 
  • Support customer-facing quality and industrialization activities, including APQP, PPAP, design reviews, process reviews, and technical audits. 
  • Build and maintain strong working relationships with OEM cell, battery pack, vehicle integration, safety, validation, manufacturing, and quality teams. 
  • Collaborate across R&D, manufacturing, quality, and intellectual-property teams to advance cell designs, application solutions, and proprietary technologies. 
  • Travel domestically and internationally up to 30% to support customer engagements, design reviews, testing, manufacturing activities, and product launches. 

Qualifications: 

  • Master’s degree in chemistry, chemical engineering, materials science, electrochemistry, or a related technical discipline. 
  • Seven or more years of experience in lithium-ion battery cell development, characterization, testing, or validation. 
  • Demonstrated experience completing at least one full lithium-ion battery cell product-development cycle, from concept and requirements definition through cell design, validation, manufacturing scale-up, production launch, and post-launch support. 
  • Hands-on experience designing, executing, and interpreting lithium-ion cell performance, life, and degradation tests. 
  • Experience with incremental capacity analysis and differential voltage analysis, including dQ/dV and dV/dQ methods. 
  • Working knowledge of electrochemical characterization techniques, including GITT, EIS, CV, and PITT. 
  • Familiarity with lithium-ion cell manufacturing processes, including electrode manufacturing, cell assembly, electrolyte filling, formation, aging, and end-of-line testing. 
  • Strong understanding of cell chemistry, material behavior, electrochemical performance, aging, and degradation mechanisms. 
  • Demonstrated ability to connect cell design and test results with manufacturing-process capability and end-product performance. 
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and root-cause-analysis skills. 
  • Ability to work effectively with global and cross-functional teams. 
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English. 

Preferred/Nice to have: 

  • Experience developing or optimizing lithium-ion cells for fast-charging applications. 
  • Knowledge of applicable battery safety standards and regulations, such as UN 38.3, UL, IEC, GB, and FMVSS requirements. 
  • Experience working directly with automotive or electric-vehicle OEM customers. 
  • Experience developing DFMEAs and PFMEAs and supporting APQP, PPAP, product qualification, change management, and customer audits. 
  • Hands-on laboratory experience with electrochemical characterization techniques such as GITT, EIS, CV, and PITT. 
  • Hands-on experience with material-characterization methods such as XRD, FTIR, Raman spectroscopy, SEM, or NMR. 
  • Experience analyzing large battery datasets using Python, MATLAB, or comparable data-analysis tools.

BESS Solution Development

  • Support the development of technical solutions for utility-scale and C&I battery energy storage projects.
  • Perform preliminary battery, power conversion system (AC/DC), MVT/HVT, auxiliary-load/ Trans, and balance-of-plant sizing.
  • Review project requirements, including power, energy, operating duration, ambient conditions, elevation, degradation, efficiency, and project life.
  • Assist in selecting appropriate battery system configurations based on customer and project requirements.
  • Prepare preliminary system configurations, equipment lists, single-line diagrams, GA Layout and technical documentation.
  • Support the evaluation of standalone energy storage, solar-plus-storage, wind-plus-storage, microgrid, and AIDC applications.

  • Identify specification gaps, design conflicts, and technical risks.
  • Maintain proposal records, technical assumptions, and customer requirements.

Technical Analysis

  • Perform or support electrical calculations related to load flow, short circuit, Arc Flash Analysis, auxiliary loads, system efficiency, and equipment ratings.
  • Assist with battery degradation, usable-energy, round-trip-efficiency, and augmentation calculations.
  • Review the capabilities of power conversion systems, including active power, reactive power, voltage support, frequency response, and fault ride-through.

  • Basic understanding of electrical systems, including transformers, switchgear, power converters, protection systems, and single-line diagrams.

We innovate in the next generation electric vehicle and energy storage technologies (lithium batteries and related systems) with the aim to accelerate electrified transportation and achieve sustainable development. Gotion is powered by a leading power battery technology company that provides solutions for vehicles including the world's first mass commercial e-bus route.

Gotion is a career destination - we are not simply attempting to just fill another job, but to pursue a dream of global green energy together! We offer outstanding opportunities to individuals seeking an exciting and challenging working environment. Everyone is highly valued and plays a vital role in the growth of our organization.

Role Summary

The Maintenance Spare Parts & Purchasing Supervisor is responsible for managing the procurement, inventory, and availability of maintenance spare parts and MRO (Maintenance, Repair, and Operations) materials. This role ensures maintenance teams have the right parts at the right time while controlling costs, maintaining accurate inventory records, and supporting equipment reliability and uptime.

  • Essential Duties and Responsibilities:
  • Manage maintenance spare parts and MRO inventory
  • Establish and maintain min/max levels and critical spare parts lists
  • Perform cycle counts and inventory audits
  • Organize and maintain parts storeroom and tool crib
  • Identify obsolete, slow-moving, and critical inventory
  • Support kitting of work orders for scheduled maintenance
  • Procure maintenance parts, tools, and services
  • Create and manage purchase orders in CMMS/ERP systems
  • Develop and manage vendor relationships
  • Negotiate pricing, lead times, and service agreements
  • Expedite critical and emergency purchases
  • Support preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance activities
  • Maintain accurate part data and BOMs in CMMS/ERP
  • Generate inventory and purchasing reports
  • Supervise and train storeroom personnel (if applicable)
  • Ensure compliance with safety and purchasing policies

Required Qualifications:

  • Associate’s degree or equivalent experience
  • 3–5 years of experience in maintenance spare parts, MRO purchasing, or storeroom management
  • Experience in manufacturing or industrial maintenance environments
  • Working knowledge of CMMS or ERP systems
  • Understanding of mechanical and electrical spare parts

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Business, or Engineering
  • Supervisory experience
  • Experience with inventory optimization and PM kitting
